{{short description|Mathematical identity involving sums of binomial coefficients}}
'''Abel's binomial theorem''', named after [[Niels Henrik Abel]], is a [[Identity (mathematics)|mathematical identity]] involving [[Summation|sums]] of [[binomial coefficient]]s. It states the following:

: <math>\sum_{k=0}^m \binom{m}{k} (w+m-k)^{m-k-1}(z+k)^k=w^{-1}(z+w+m)^m.</math>

==Example==
===The case ''m'' = 2===
: <math>
\begin{align}
& {} \quad \binom{2}{0}(w+2)^1(z+0)^0+\binom{2}{1}(w+1)^0(z+1)^1+\binom{2}{2}(w+0)^{-1}(z+2)^2 \\
& = (w+2)+2(z+1)+\frac{(z+2)^2}{w} \\
& = \frac{(z+w+2)^2}{w}.
\end{align}
</math>
